description: Three-wheeled open-sided auto rickshaw with a single front wheel, handlebar steering and a rear bench under a curved canopy.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Three-wheeled auto rickshaw, single front wheel with handlebar steering, rounded front cowl and headlamp, open sides with a curved canopy roof over a rear passenger bench, chrome bar frame and rear luggage rack Materials: Glossy two-tone enamel with chrome trim, polished stainless canopy edge, scuffed rubber floor mat, worn vinyl bench, exhaust soot at the rear.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 3,244/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, one 256 px canvas at 0.3 MB, factory 108 ms. Turntable: enclosed background is the open cabin, allowed on measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 1.34 x 1.95 x 2.95 m against a declared 1.40 x 1.95 x 2.90; the proxy agrees with the declaration (1 : 0.662 : 0.449) and every station is its fraction.
featureReviews.notes: Canopy 0.21-0.79 L, rear pillar at 0.79-0.85 L, bars 0.60 H, front wheel 0.00-0.17 L, rear wheels 0.65-0.82 L -- all off the occupancy map. THE PROXY'S UPPER BANDS ARE NOT EVIDENCE HERE and were not chased: the ten-band table reads reference depth 1.008 at band 6, 0.302 at band 7, 0.348 at band 8 and 0.878 at band 9, i.e. a machine that necks to 0.59 m front-to-back between two full-length sections and flares out again. No tuk-tuk does that; it is Meshy losing four thin canopy pillars, which is the documented failure mode on separated thin members, and bands 7-8 are exactly the open cabin where the only geometry IS those pillars. The band table decided the spirit house in this same session and is the right instrument when the proxy is coherent -- it is not coherent here, and the plate comparison is.

featureReviews.evidence: Green side walls rising 0.70 -> 0.94 toward the tail, a solid rear wall behind the bench, a pair of 45 mm GREEN rear canopy pillars, a thin chrome front pillar, belt and edge rails, bench and back, driver's saddle and footboard, chrome basket on the tail.
featureReviews.notes: The first build carried the canopy on four thin chrome sticks over a 0.32 m tub and read as a frame with no body: the plate's cabin is enclosed to above the seat cushion and its REAR pillars are green bodywork, not chrome. Two further faults came out of the 270 view rather than any gate -- the tub bottom sat at 0.30 while the checker floor was at 0.17, so a 1.24 x 1.50 m plate hung out below the bodywork on both sides and the prop read as a scooter standing on a pallet; and the body stopped at z 0.02 leaving a gap to the nose that the driver's footboard floated in. The tub now runs from z 0.74 to the tail with its bottom at 0.15. The turntable's enclosed backdrop is the open cabin, allowed on the _holecc measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Three instanced wheels, tyre #3a3025 with a chrome hub at 40% of the tyre radius, measured off the plate (hub 84 px across a 212 px tyre). One lathe, three instances.
featureReviews.notes: The wheels rendered as PALE GREY PLATES and two separate things were behind it. `wheelGeo` interpolates the rim colour outward from rRim to the tread, so the whole sidewall is a gradient from hub tone to tyre tone -- shrinking the rim only made the pale gradient wider. `rimBand` (default unchanged, so every other vehicle is byte-identical: verified against the shipped songthaew bundle at max |diff| 0 over position AND colour) stops the chrome at the hub cap. And the old tyre #4d4b46 sat INSIDE the turntable gate's backdrop test at luma 75 (|d| 17 <= 24) and saturation 0.09 (<= 0.16); it is held on CHROMA now at luma 52, saturation 0.36.

featureReviews.evidence: Green #2d6542 and yellow #e1ad10 as measured, both vertex colours on one gloss material.
featureReviews.notes: Yellow band on the nose and stripe on the tub as the plate has them.

name: Tuk-tuk
notes: Sized on the Bangkok tourist tuk-tuk rather than the larger cargo samlor. Open-sided, so the interior bench and floor are visible from every angle and cannot be faked with a closed shell. No destruction groups: the canopy is a welded bar frame, not a removable assembly.
